2.2 Where it fits

This book is one of nine on the FirstPair photo tools. Each owns one part, and The FirstPair Photo Stack shows how they fit together.

  • tiffgraph walks a TIFF or DNG file’s structure under a fixed grammar and finds its editable XMP packet.
  • phidentify computes a photo’s identities: SHA-256, DNG raw blocks, image data, Lightroom fingerprint, metadata record and preserved digest.
  • phindex keeps those identities for every file of a volume, and aligns two volumes by content.
  • DNG Compare compares pairs and preserves one side byte for byte as deltas against the other, with a searchable metadata section, through dngc.
  • Semantic Unison synchronizes photo trees, sending metadata edits without resending image bytes, and preserves what a shuttle disk brings into the same archives.
  • packdir keeps directories of small files as SQLite archives that still work like plain files.
  • Tursolite is the SQLite and Turso layer under packdir, DNG Compare and Mechanic.
  • diskproxy serves a folder as a virtual disk, such as previews with camera metadata spliced in, and captures ratings into sidecars.
  • Lightroom Repair repairs Lightroom Classic catalogs, previews and Sync without forging their state.

DNG Compare owns two contracts the other books rely on: the archive layout (Part II), which Semantic Unison writes too, and the engine rule: metadata records made by Perl ExifTool and by exiftool-rs are separate identities and are never mixed in one archive.
